46.0.0.en: 1- God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.

46.0.1.en: 1- The Church and every soul that believes in God face war from the demons, in addition to the visible enemies, who are the wicked stirred up against her by the demons; but God offers His protection to the Church in three forms:

46.0.2.en: a- Refuge: that is, a fortress in which His children take shelter, so that no one can harm them, however strong he may be.

46.0.3.en: b- Strength: so that the children of God can conquer all their enemies through Him.

46.0.4.en: c- Help: that is, a supporter of His children spiritually, psychologically and physically, so that they remain steadfast in the battle and are never shaken.

46.0.5.en: 2- The Church's past experiences with God confirm her faith, for God has been found exceedingly strong in troubles, that is, a supporter of His children throughout history and a deliverer of them from troubles that could not be passed through by reason; indeed He also glorified them, and they praised God.

46.1.0.en: 2- Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea;

46.1.1.en: 1- The writer of the psalm affirms the steadfastness of the children of God, whatever changes occur around them, even if they are powerful natural changes, such as earthquakes that move the earth; yet the children of God remain steadfast, and whatever the circumstances change, or the principles and values around them are shaken, they continue in their faith and their sound spiritual conduct.

46.1.2.en: 2- Then he presents a natural change that is hard to imagine, namely the overturning of the mountains, which are the strongest and most stable thing on earth. If these mountains were to fall into the midst of the seas, the children of God would remain steadfast in their faith; that is, if the strongest powers of the world were overturned and sank in the seas, or if the great ones, even the religious leaders, were plunged into the lusts of the world and drowned in them, the true children of God would remain in their spiritual steadfastness, as happened when religious leaders fell into heresies, such as Nestorius, Eutyches and Arius.

46.1.3.en: 3- The removal of the earth is a type of the earthquake that occurred at the crucifixion of Christ, announcing the turmoil of the world and its need of the Redeemer and Savior.

46.2.0.en: 3- Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with the swelling thereof. Selah.

46.2.1.en: Roar: the voices of the waves rise.

46.2.2.en: Be troubled: the waters surge and run so swiftly that they hinder the passage of ships and boats.

46.2.3.en: Swelling thereof: its rising and greatness.

46.2.4.en: 1- The writer of the psalm affirms that our God is our refuge even if the earth is removed and the mountains are overturned. Likewise he says in this verse, even if the waters of the seas move with great force and their voices rise, as happens in floods, and even if the mountains become greater in their great height, all this will not shake the faith of the children of God who take refuge in Him, for He is their refuge and strength.

46.2.5.en: 2- The mountains are a type of the mighty and the great ones in this world, and the waters are a type of the multitude of people, or of the multitude of armies, such as the Assyrian army which attacked Jerusalem in the days of King Hezekiah. All these cause no turmoil in the hearts of the children of God who are steadfast in faith in Him.

46.2.6.en: 3- He says the word Selah at the end of the verse, which is a musical pause, so that a person may contemplate the power of God, the fortified refuge, and no longer be disturbed by the turmoil of the world.

46.2.7.en: Take refuge in God when things are in turmoil around you, so that your heart is not shaken with them, but stands firm in your faith and remembers the power of God that supports you; and as your prayers increase you will experience the help of God and feel His presence with you.

46.3.0.en: 4- There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High.

46.3.1.en: 1- The children of God who take refuge in their God, who is their refuge, are not troubled by the shaking of the world around them, but enjoy the work of the Holy Spirit in them, who is a river whose streams make glad the city of God. These streams are the gifts and fruits of the Holy Spirit, who works in the believers within the Church, which is the city of God. The Church is the holiest place in the world; in her the Most High God dwells, and He abides and dwells in His believing children who are united to Him through His holy sacraments. This verse is a prophecy about the work of the Holy Spirit in the believers in the New Testament (Jn 7:37-39).

46.3.2.en: 2- The Holy Spirit, who is the river, has as His streams the Apostles, the priests who are their successors, and the servants, who preach the word of God and make glad the city of God, which is the Church. The river's water is sweet and flows quietly, unlike the salty sea whose waters roar and surge; so the work of the Holy Spirit is calm and restful within believing souls, and He works in service with spirituality and calm.

46.3.3.en: 3- The Holy Spirit, who is the river, continues to work in the Church until He raises her to heaven, where the dwellings of the Most High God abide forever, and there the believers enjoy God with an enjoyment that cannot be expressed. And they delight in holiness in the holy place of the tabernacles of the Most High, that is, the place that the Holy Spirit sanctified, that the children of God may dwell in it forever.

46.3.4.en: 4- The streams are also the baptisms which the Holy Spirit has granted to His churches, so that the souls of the believers rejoice in the new members, and are sanctified as dwellings of the Most High God, and are established in His Church forever.

46.4.0.en: 5- God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.

46.4.1.en: 1- God's dwelling in the midst of His Church keeps her from being shaken before the world's opposition and persecutions against her, because God in her midst protects her and strengthens His children who live in the world yet remain holding fast to His commandments, however much evil opposes them.

46.4.2.en: 2- God helps His children in the Old Testament until the morning comes, which is the incarnation of Christ the Savior, so that they enjoy His salvation, in the hope of which they lived and died. He also helps all who believe in Him "right early," that is, Christ in His Second Coming on the day of judgment, when He justifies them by His blood. So God helps them on the way of their spiritual striving until they reach the Kingdom.

46.5.0.en: 6- The heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved: he uttered his voice, the earth melted.

46.5.1.en: 1- The pagan nations, headed by the Roman state, tried to resist Christianity, and persecuted the Church after the Jewish persecution, but God turned the persecutions into strength which the Church received. On the other hand the kingdoms melted, that is, the Roman Empire melted within the Church when Constantine ascended the throne of the Roman state, and attended the First Ecumenical Council at Nicaea.

46.5.2.en: 2- When Christ cried out on the Cross and said, "It is finished," the earth melted, that is, an earthquake occurred, the veil of the Temple was torn, and the tombs were opened, because Christ had accomplished the redemption (Mt 27:51; Mk 15:37, 38).

46.5.3.en: 3- The nations resisted the Church but submitted to her after this. Then Christ comes in His Second Coming and utters His voice to judge the world, and the earth melts before Him, and the wicked try to hide from His face; then He glorifies His children in His Kingdom, and casts the wicked into eternal torment (2 Pet 3:10).

46.6.0.en: 7- The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.

46.6.1.en: The writer ends his words about the steadfastness of the children of God by reassuring them that God is very strong, because He is the Lord of hosts, meaning the heavenly hosts, of which only one is able to kill the army of the Assyrians in the days of King Hezekiah. The mighty God is the refuge of His children and His people, who are Jacob, or Israel, and then the Christians in the New Testament. He ends this verse with the word Selah, so that the reader may contemplate God, the supporter and the one who establishes His children.

46.6.2.en: The Holy Spirit dwelling in you is able to establish you and support you in all situations, however difficult; so do not worry, and do not think about tomorrow, because God who supports you dwells in you forever.

46.7.0.en: 8- Come, behold the works of the LORD, what desolations he hath made in the earth. 9- He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; he burneth the chariot in the fire.

46.7.1.en: 1- God, who dwells in the midst of His people, triumphed over the nations around them and laid them waste, broke their weapons and burned them with fire, and crushed the armies of the enemies, so the earth around His people became quiet. This happened in the days of David and before him, that is, the days of Joshua and Moses. Thus God's superiority over all the gods of the pagan nations appeared, and His victory over them. Therefore the writer calls all peoples, and even the children of God themselves, to contemplate the power of God, victorious over the enemies.

46.7.2.en: 2- In a moment, when Christ died on the Cross, He bound Satan, laid waste his kingdom, and broke and burned his weapons, that is, they became worthless before the power of God dwelling in His children, because the Holy Spirit dwelt in them through the sacrament of the Holy Myron, and by this the earth became calm and the children of God lived in peace. The souls that believe in Christ are not disturbed by the wars and weapons of Satan, because God who dwells in them lays waste these lusts which fight against them, and gives His children virtues in their place.

46.7.3.en: 3- On the day of judgment Christ nullifies the power of the demons and utterly lays waste his kingdom by casting him into eternal torment, and His children dwell with Him in the Kingdom, enjoying His fellowship forever.

46.8.0.en: 10- Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth. 11- The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.

46.8.1.en: 1- At the close of this psalm the writer asks the believers to cease from base lusts, and also from fear of the demons and their wars and all the powers of evil, for they are worthless before the power of God; and to cease also from relying on the passing and weak powers of men, that their reliance may be on God alone.

46.8.2.en: 2- He also asks the believers to be lifted up with Christ who was crucified and then ascended into heaven, so that they leave their earthly concerns and busy themselves with the heavenly life, that is, that they have a spiritual way of life.

46.8.3.en: 3- He affirms at the end of the psalm that God, the Lord of hosts, is with us, and that He gives victory to His people in every generation. We have already explained the last verse in the explanation of (v. 7).

46.8.4.en: That you may conquer your enemies the demons, may you fix your eyes and your heart on Christ, so that you are not disturbed by the power of the enemies; lift yourself up and leave your evil lusts by repentance, and you will behold the work of God in you and rejoice in it. The shout: God the King of the earth. To the chief musician. For the sons of Korah. A psalm: "O clap your hands, all ye people") ... v. 1) Introduction:

46.8.5.en: 1- Its writer: the sons of Korah.

46.8.7.en: a- When David brought the Ark of the Covenant back to Jerusalem (1 Sam 6:19-21).

46.8.8.en: b- A prophecy about God's victory over Sennacherib and his army (2 Kgs 18:13-19:37).

46.8.9.en: c- A prophecy about the redemption of Christ, which was accomplished on the Cross, so that He reigned over all who believe in Him from among the Gentiles and the Jews.

46.8.10.en: d- A prophecy about the ascension of Christ into heaven (v. 5).

46.8.11.en: e- A prophecy about the Second Coming of Christ on the day of judgment, to reign over those who believe in Him from the whole earth.

46.8.12.en: 3- The Jews used to chant this psalm at the Feast of Trumpets (Num 29:1) and their great feasts.

46.8.13.en: 4- In the Coptic Orthodox Church the priest recites it after the end of the Liturgy, as he goes around the altar and claps his hands to glorify God.

46.8.14.en: 5- Some churches recite this psalm on the feasts of the Theophany and the Ascension.

46.8.15.en: 6- This psalm is suited to every soul that loves God and longs for Him to reign over her, so she praises Him that longing for Him may be renewed in her heart.

46.8.16.en: 7- This psalm is one of the psalms of praise, like the psalm before it and the one after it.

46.8.17.en: 8- This psalm is considered one of the Messianic psalms.

46.8.18.en: 9- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Agpeya at the Third Hour, in which the Holy Spirit descended upon the disciples, in order to glorify God who reigned over His Church and those who believe in Him.

47.0.0.en: 1- O clap your hands, all ye nations; shout unto God with the voice of triumph.

47.0.1.en: 1- The writer of the psalm calls the whole world to believe in God and praise Him, and to express its joy by clapping its hands, and also by shouting, that is, praising with a loud voice.

47.0.2.en: 2- Clapping of hands is a type of good works, by which the believer expresses his love for God, and when people see his good works they glorify God, so that the believer's words are mingled with his works, and when others glorify God they love Him and submit to Him; that is, the believer can draw those around him to the worship of God.

47.1.0.en: 2- For the LORD most high is terrible; he is a great King over all the earth.

47.1.1.en: In this verse he describes God as high, that is, exalted above all the pagan gods, all men and all heavenly and earthly creatures. He describes Him also as terrible, that is, feared by those in heaven and on earth, and he likewise names Him a great King over all the earth, that is, everything is under His authority; and there is no king on earth to whom all the nations have submitted except Christ, in whom many have believed from every place in the world.

47.1.2.en: You are a light to the world, and you must glorify God in your life by your good works and your upright speech, and by this you draw souls to God; and take care lest you be a stumbling block to anyone, and drive them away from God.

47.2.0.en: 3- He shall subdue the people under us, and the nations under our feet.

47.2.1.en: 1- By the Cross Christ accomplished redemption, so all the peoples of the Jews, that is, their tribes, submitted to Him, namely the believers converted from the Jews. Likewise many of the pagan nations believed in Him. All these submitted to the preaching of the Apostles, who led them in the way of faith, so they learned humility, abandoning their philosophies and boasting in their lineages.

47.2.2.en: 2- Likewise Christ gave His disciples and those who believe in Him authority over the demons, so that they tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy (Lk 10:19), and cast out the demons who held sway over men; in addition to giving the believers power to repel all the thoughts of the demons.

47.2.3.en: 3- The submission to God of the peoples and nations increases in the souls consecrated to Christ, whether in the priesthood, or monasticism, or any service.

47.3.0.en: 4- He shall choose our inheritance for us, the excellency of Jacob whom he loved. Selah.

47.3.1.en: 1- God chose His people to give them His promises, and out of His love He chose for them their portion, which is God Himself, and poured out His blessings on them; He gave them the land of Canaan, and blessed their crops, their cattle and all their possessions, so they were distinguished from the other peoples by God's dwelling in their midst and His protection of them.

47.3.2.en: 2- God chose His people, the descendants of Jacob, who loved the birthright, that is, heavenly things. But Esau preferred the lentils, that is, material things. So Jacob boasted in God and God boasted in him, and Jacob became the portion of the Lord, and God became an inheritance for him.

47.3.3.en: 3- The writer ends the verse with the word Selah, which is a musical pause for contemplating the love of God, and consequently the response of His people to Him.

47.3.4.en: How beautiful it is that your portion should be the Lord, so that you think of Him and are occupied with Him, and repeat His psalms every day, and taste the sweetness of fellowship with Him, and even enjoy seeing Him in your life, and live the Kingdom while you are on earth.

47.4.0.en: 5- God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.

47.4.1.en: The trumpet (shofar): a musical instrument, a horn made from the horn of an animal, that is, a wind instrument used in worship.

47.4.2.en: This verse is a clear prophecy about Christ, who conquered death, rose from the dead, and ascended into the heavens before the eyes of His disciples, who worshipped Him and then returned to Jerusalem with great joy, glorifying and praising God (Lk 24:21-53). And when Christ was lifted up into heaven the angels received Him with joy, which is expressed here by the sound of the trumpet. And at His Second Coming the angels will sound the trumpet, announcing His arrival (1 Thess 4:16).

47.5.0.en: 6- Sing praises to God, sing praises: sing praises unto our King, sing praises. 7- For God is the King of all the earth: sing a poem.

47.5.1.en: 1- Because of the greatness of the divine ascension into heaven, which means the possibility of mankind's ascending and entering the places that were closed since the expulsion of Adam, so that it becomes the right of those who believe in Christ to enter Paradise and then the Kingdom, for all this the psalm calls all readers to sing praises to God, who is King over all the earth. But at the same time it calls Him in (v. 6) "our King," that is, although He is King over all the earth because He created it, He especially gives the believers in Him the enjoyment of His reign over their hearts, to give them His special blessings, the most important of which is His dwelling in their hearts.

47.5.2.en: 2- This singing is to be in the form of a poem, that is, melodious verse with great meanings, so the writer asks that the singing be with understanding, and he repeats the word "sing praises" four times in (v. 6), which is a type of the four corners of the world, that is, he calls the whole earth to sing praises to God; and this draws the hearts of those who believe in Christ to the heaven into which He ascended, and consequently they live a heavenly life.

47.5.3.en: Praise lifts your heart to heaven and looses your chains that bind you to the lusts of the world; so be diligent in hymns and praises, that you may live with God and glorify Him, and He may bless you.

47.6.0.en: 8- God reigneth over the heathen: God sitteth upon the throne of his holiness.

47.6.1.en: 1- God reigned on the Cross when He died to redeem all mankind, and He reigned over the hearts of those who believed from the pagan nations, as He reigned over the hearts of those converted from the Jews. For God sanctified and purified the hearts of those who believe in Him by Baptism, and sat in them, so they are the throne of His holiness.

47.6.2.en: 2- The throne of God's holiness is the four living creatures who are not incarnate; this is the heavenly throne. But Christ in His humility was born in the manger and crucified on the Cross, and by this humility of His He made the heart of the least believer in Him a throne on which He sits. And the reigning of God means that He takes care of the whole man and blesses him, and sitting means continuance and permanence in the heart of man.

47.7.0.en: 9- The princes of the people are gathered together, even the people of the God of Abraham: for God is the shield of the earth; he is greatly exalted. Shields: plural of shield, the large buckler. The shield is a defensive instrument which the soldier uses in war to ward off arrows from his body.

47.7.1.en: 1- The princes of the people are the great ones of the peoples who believed in Christ, and many of them became servants and preachers. These gathered together, and with them also those converted from Jewish origin; all these are the people of the God of Abraham, because Abraham is the father of the Jews and the Gentiles, and everyone who lived by the faith of Abraham and did his works and accepted faith in Christ enjoyed the salvation of Christ.

47.7.2.en: 2- God in His love is a shield, that is, a protection for the whole earth. What is meant is protection for all who believe in Him in the whole earth. And God is greatly exalted, that is, above all the pagan gods and likewise the earthly kings; therefore whoever believes in Him enjoys complete protection and no harm touches him.

47.7.3.en: God is able to protect you from any things that harm you, so why are you disturbed by the changes of the world? Take refuge in Him and hold fast to Him always, and He will turn everything to your good and nullify the plot of the demons directed against you, and if you fall He raises you up and supports you.

47.7.4.en: The city of God. A song and psalm for the sons of Korah: "Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised") ... v. 1) Introduction:

47.7.5.en: 1- The writers of this psalm are the sons of Korah.

47.7.6.en: 2- It speaks about the city of God, that is, Zion, which is a type of the Church of the New Testament, and it contemplates her beauty and her great attributes.

47.7.7.en: 3- Perhaps this psalm is a prophecy about the defeat of Sennacherib before the walls of Jerusalem, which God protected (vv. 4-6).

47.7.8.en: 4- Perhaps this psalm is also a prophecy about the victory of Jehoshaphat over three kings, the children of Ammon, Moab and Edom, who were terrified before the city of God, while the people of God were praising and glorifying God (2 Chr 20:1-30).

47.7.9.en: 5- It is a psalm of praise and thanksgiving to God like the two psalms before it: Psalm 46 speaks to us about God the refuge, Psalm 47 speaks to us about God the King, and this psalm speaks to us about God in His great city.

47.7.10.en: 6- This psalm is not found in the prayer of the Agpeya.
